ALTERNATIVE SOURCES OF CROW INDIAN INCOME
Agriculture
There are only a few small tracts of tribal land in the area proposed for mining and most of the surface is now owned by Westmoreland Resources. Therefore, little agricultural income could be expected by the Tribe as an alternate source of income if coal leasing were not pursued.
Also, since most of the surface does not belong to the Tribe little income could be expected from recreational activities or timber harvest.

Oil, Gas, Metallic and Non-Metallic Minerals Development
The development of the coal will not affect future development of oil and gas resources, if such exist. They would be at much greater depth and recoverable whether the coal is mined or not. The Tongue River Member of the Fort Union Formation in this area contains no potential metallic mineral resources that would constitute a future source of income for the Crow Tribe.
Other than coal the only non-metallic minerals of the area that might have any future economic potential are gravel, clinker, and bloating clays.
Production of these materials would create adverse environmental impacts associated with land disturbance, and beneficial impacts associated with income opportunities.
